name: Brahmapureeswarar Temple, Thirukkuvalai
deity: Shiva as Brahmapureeswarar, with the Thyagaraja processional deity Avani Vidangar
period: A Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram; the stone temple of the Chola age
summary: At Thirukkuvalai in the Kaveri delta, Shiva stands as Brahmapureeswarar, and the Thyagaraja of the shrine — Avani Vidangar — is one of the seven dancing Thyagarajas of the delta, whose procession is said to move in the Bhringa Natanam.

sections.history: Thirukkuvalai lies among the paddy country of the Kaveri delta, in the Nagapattinam–Thiruvarur region. Its temple to Shiva as Brahmapureeswarar is a Paadal Petra Sthalam sung in the Tevaram, its stone shrines of the Chola age. The temple is one of the Sapta Vidanga Sthalams, and its Thyagaraja is honoured as Avani Vidangar, one of the seven Vidangas of the dancing tradition of the delta.
sections.architecture: Built in the Dravidian manner, the temple gathers around the sanctum of Brahmapureeswarar, with the Somaskanda Thyagaraja — Shiva with Uma and the child Skanda — worshipped as the uncarved Vidanga and carried as the processional lord. Pillared halls and a gateway tower open before the sanctum in the delta manner of the Chola and later centuries.
sections.legends: The Sapta Vidanga temples share the legend of the uncarved Thyagaraja images, worshipped in the Somaskanda form and each moving in its own dance when carried in procession. At Thirukkuvalai the Thyagaraja is Avani Vidangar, and his procession is said to move in the Bhringa Natanam, the dance likened to the hovering of a bee.
sections.festivals: The temple keeps the festivals of Shiva and the processions of the Vidangar through the year, with the days of the Nayanmar saints observed in the village shrine, and the procession of the dancing Thyagaraja at the heart of its celebration.
sections.experience: Thirukkuvalai is a quiet delta temple among the seven dancing Thyagarajas, rewarding for the pilgrim who follows the Vidanga shrines through the paddy country. It joins the other six — from Thiruvarur to Vedaranyam — into the single pilgrimage of the seven dances.

visit.timings: Open daily with morning and evening darshan sessions and a midday closure; festival days and processions are busiest. Confirm current timings before visiting.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional dress is expected — shoulders and knees covered; footwear removed before entering. Men are traditionally asked to remove the upper garment before the sanctum, as at many southern shrines; follow the posted rules.
visit.photography: Photography is restricted in and around the sanctum; follow the posted rules and the priests' guidance.
visit.gettingThere: Thirukkuvalai lies in the Kaveri delta in the Nagapattinam–Thiruvarur region, reached by road from the surrounding delta towns.
